title: Condon worked with Manhattan Project figures

tellings.difference: Where Grusch says only "Condon was involved", Jesse Michels names specific roles: helping Oppenheimer choose Los Alamos and helping draft the McMahon Atomic Energy Act. He also mentions the Los Alamos Primer.
tellings.link_reason: Both tellings are about Edward Condon's part in the 1940s Manhattan Project and atomic-energy work alongside figures like Oppenheimer. The telling gives his roles there in more detail, but it covers the same subject at the same scope.

as_told.title: Condon's Manhattan Project role and choice of Los Alamos
as_told.place_text: Los Alamos, New Mexico; Göttingen, Germany

plain: In the 1940s, the physicist Edward Condon is said to have worked closely with leaders of the Manhattan Project, the US wartime program to build the atomic bomb. David Grusch, a former intelligence officer, says only that "Condon was involved". He mentions Vannevar Bush, the wartime head of US science. Jesse Michels gives more detail as his own framing. He says Condon is sometimes credited with helping J. Robert Oppenheimer, the head of the bomb project, choose Los Alamos as its site. He also says Condon helped draft the McMahon Atomic Energy Act, the law that put atomic matters under civilian control, and he mentions an early bomb-project text called the Los Alamos Primer. In a later episode Michels adds that Condon and Oppenheimer were very close, and that Condon spent time in Göttingen, Germany, with the physicist Max Born. Michels and Grusch raise it to tie Condon to the secrecy culture of the bomb project.
